extracted.intended_audience: fiction writers (novelists and short-story authors) seeking story-structure guidance
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for constructing and evaluating fiction using a three-act plot model and named plot points (Hook, Inciting Event, First Plot Point, Midpoint, Third Plot Point, Climax, Resolution) plus supporting structural concepts.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Hook
rubrics_metrics.description: "A question" that engages readers from the opening.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The opening should immediately pose a question or present a compelling element that draws readers in. The Hook functions to engage curiosity and set up stakes right away.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inciting Event
rubrics_metrics.description: An event that initiates the story's central conflict.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This beat must introduce the central problem or change that forces the protagonist's life out of balance and sets the story in motion.

rubrics_metrics.name: First Plot Point
rubrics_metrics.description: Creates "a seismic shift" launching escalating tension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The First Plot Point should pivot the story from setup to escalation by introducing new priorities or obstacles that commit the protagonist to the main conflict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Midpoint
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Midpoint converts passive response into active pursuit — a turning point that changes the protagonist's approach and raises the stakes or clarity of goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third Plot Point
rubrics_metrics.description: Transitions through false victory to the low moment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This beat should upend any apparent victory and propel the protagonist into their lowest, most vulnerable place prior to the climax; it prepares emotional and plot conditions for final confrontation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Climax
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Climax is the decisive confrontation where the protagonist must sacrifice something significant; the outcome is a true gain or loss that resolves the central conflict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides closure in the "new normal world."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After the climax, the Resolution should show how the world (and the protagonist) has changed and establish the story's new equilibrium, closing remaining threads appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chiastic Structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Links major beats: Hook ↔ Resolution, Inciting Event ↔ Climax, First ↔ Third Plot Points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use mirrored/paired beats to create a satisfying structural symmetry; corresponding beats across the story should reflect and invert one another to reinforce themes and pacing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Four Metaphoric Worlds
rubrics_metrics.description: Normal World (Act 1), Adventure World (Act 2), Underworld (Act 3), New Normal (Resolution).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Map acts to distinct ‘worlds’ metaphorically to clarify shifts in tone, stakes, and character state: Act 1 establishes normal, Act 2 moves into adventure, Act 3 into an underworld/lowest point, then the new normal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pinch Points
rubrics_metrics.description: Critical moments often neglected yet "crucial to your story structure."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and strengthen pinch points — moments that remind readers of the antagonist/pressure and heighten tension — as they are essential to sustaining momentum and clarity of conflict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importance of Story Structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Story structure is "the single most important factor for a writer's success."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat structure as foundational: applying these beats and concepts allows authors to craft stories that 'work' reliably. Prioritize structural clarity when planning, revising, or evaluating a manuscript.
